articles.summary: Rafael Louzán toma la palabra: Es el sorteo en memoria de Jesús de Miguel. Todo el cariño para su familia. Se buscaba el objetivo de la proximidad geo
articles.body:
Última hora del sorteo de Copa del Rey, en directo

A las 12:30 horas se definen 28 nuevas eliminatorias de la Copa del Rey, cuyos emparejamientos estarán condicionados por dos criterios establecidos en las bases de competición: el enfrentamiento, siempre que sea posible, entre equipos de inferior y superior categoría , y la proximidad geográfica , que en esta ronda reducirá de cuatro a dos los grupos territoriales, con una distribución de norte y sur que incluye a 36 y 20 clubes, respectivamente.

articles.title: Diego Simeone: Atletico Madrid boss breaks La Liga victories record
articles.summary: Diego Simeone records his 345th La Liga victory as Atletico Madrid manager to set a new mark.
articles.body:
Atletico Madrid's 3-0 victory over Getafe may have been routine, but the win was another landmark in manager Diego Simeone's lengthy tenure at the club.

Sunday's triumph at Estadio Coliseum was the Argentine's 345th La Liga win in his 567th match, surpassing the record for the most victories in the Spanish top flight.

Simeone beat the mark of legendary former Atletico and Spain manager Luis Aragones, who won 344 matches but needed 189 more games to reach that total.

"It makes me happy," Simeone said of setting the new mark, with his side now third in the table after 10 wins from 13 games.

"I don't usually find many things to be happy about, but there is an incredible amount of work behind this."

Questioned about the perception that his team are defensive, Simeone said that was a "constant criticism we face".

He added: "I don't place much value on it, but I do take note of it.

"This narrative that we're a defensive team, as if we're always playing solely to defend. You don't win 345 matches just by defending. Is that even possible?"

The 56-year-old has been in charge of Atletico since December 2011, joining the club in an era when Jose Mourinho's Real Madrid and Pep Guardiola's Barcelona were the dominant teams in Spain.

He outlasted the pair of managerial superstars, leading Atletico into a period of consistent success and staying with his side long enough to witness Mourinho's return to Real this summer, 13 years after his initial departure.

Having won the Europa League in May 2012, after his appointment on 23 December 2011, Simeone led Atletico to the European Super Cup title three months later.

He then won the Copa del Rey in his first full season and secured the club's first La Liga title since 1996 - when Simeone was an Atletico player - in the following campaign.

Atletico have established themselves as the third force in Spanish football under his leadership, qualifying for the Champions League in every full season under his charge.

However he has been unable to win European football's premier competition, losing in the final to city rivals Real twice in heart-breaking fashion - in extra-time in 2014 after Real scored a stoppage-time equaliser, and on penalties in 2016.

Simeone's last silverware arrived in 2021 when he won a second Spanish league championship, while he also guided the team to a Europa League and Super Cup double in 2018.

His contract expires at the end of this season with the Atletico fanbase now waiting to see if their manager intends to extend his remarkable victory record into another campaign.

There has been an evolution since Simeone arrived, but his peak came when his players were happy to defend without the ball, deep in their own box. That is how the titles arrived.

He has not found the same effort or quality with a squad built to attack. In the peak years he found the perfect balance between deep defence and counterattack, yet picking it is harder now that his team must take the initiative.

None of that diminishes his legacy. He turned the club's mentality into a winning one and sustained it for over a decade, the two hardest things in football.

After losing a second Champions League final to Real Madrid in 2016 he could have left, but he renewed his energy.

Atletico have flirted with Luis Enrique and Unai Emery, yet everyone agrees he goes when he decides. For now, he finds plenty of reasons to stay.

articles.title: CAS decision on Senegal’s AFCON 2025 title appeal on Tuesday
articles.summary: Senegal are contesting CAF’s decision to declare Morocco champions, despite Senegal winning the final 1-0 in January.
articles.body:
The Court of Arbitration ‌for Sport (CAS) will release its decision on Senegal’s appeal against ⁠being stripped of ⁠this year’s Africa Cup of Nations (AFCON) title on Tuesday.

Senegal are contesting the decision of the Confederation of African Football (CAF) to declare Morocco champions , despite Senegal ⁠beating the hosts 1-0 in extra time in January’s final in Rabat, and the outcome will be announced on Tuesday, the court confirmed on Monday.

It did not give a time for the announcement.

CAS heard the arguments of Senegal, Morocco and CAF in Lausanne ⁠in early October.

It had initially promised a decision within days of the hearing on ‌October 8 but then decided to issue a complete ruling, including legal grounds, known as a CAS Award. That process requires several weeks.

CAS Awards hold the same value as a national court judgement, enforceable in accordance with the New York Convention on the Recognition and Enforcement of Foreign Arbitral Awards. Awards may be enforced by sports federations or state courts, depending on the circumstances.

In the final , Senegal ⁠ walked off the pitch for 14 minutes after a penalty ⁠was awarded against them late in regulation time, with several players returning to the dressing room in protest before they resumed play.

Morocco missed the spot kick, sending the match into extra time, where Senegal ⁠scored the winner to secure victory.

However, they were stripped of the title two months later after CAF’s Appeal Board ruled ⁠that Senegal had forfeited the match by walking off ⁠the pitch, overturning the result and awarding a 3-0 victory to Morocco.

Senegal appealed the CAF ruling to sport’s highest court, CAS, on March 25, but it was heard some six months later. The ‌basis of its arguments is that the referee’s decision is final and he allowed the match to be completed.

The CAS panel is presided over by French sports law ‌expert ‌Gerald Simon, with assistance from Italian international law professor Luigi Fumagalli and Hamburg-based lawyer and professor of law at the University of Zurich, Ulrich Haas.

articles.title: B/R's 2026 College Football Playoff Bracket Projections and Predictions after Week 12
articles.summary: Conference championship games are looming, but the final weekend of the regular season will provide some clarity for the 2026 College Football Playoff.
articles.body:
Conference championship games are looming, but the final weekend of the regular season will provide some clarity for the 2026 College Football Playoff.

If there are a few significant upsets, that clarity could be delayed. But if most of the nation's top-ranked teams navigate this rivalry-filled week, several of those programs will essentially lock in their CFP invitation.

First-round byes remain at stake, however.

Even if a team has a notable margin for error—Georgia or Utah, as examples—locking in the best possible seeding in the Playoff is essential.

The projected bracket is a reflection of B/R's Top 25 dropped into the organization of the official CFP format.

What a wild Saturday in the Big Ten. Nebraska ended a 31-game losing streak against Top 25 competition, also eliminating Ohio State from the conference and CFP races in the process. Upsets by Michigan and Washington cracked the Big Ten standings wide open—especially for Oregon. More on that later.

Because of these two results, the ACC Championship Game is locked in. Wake Forest continued its hot streak in Week 12, at one point building a 36-point lead at Georgia Tech. Miami recovered from an early 14-0 deficit and outlasted rival Virginia Tech. The main question between now and this showdown is whether Miami wideout Malachi Toney will be able to return from an ankle injury in time.

Georgia and Utah clinched berths in their respective conference championship games and probably secured spots in the CFP as well. At the very least, both are guaranteed a shot at an automatic bid.

1. Georgia 2. Utah 3. Notre Dame 4. Miami 5. Texas 6. Tennessee 7. Alabama 8. Wake Forest 9. Texas Tech 10. UCLA 11. BYU 12. Iowa 13. Indiana 14. Oregon 15. USC 16. Arizona 17. Houston 18. Louisville 19. Liberty 20. Florida 21. Boise State 22. Oklahoma 23. New Mexico 24. Auburn 25. Air Force

Seeding is a reflection of how B/R's Top 25 would shape the bracket.

Power 4 Champions and Top Group of 6 Team

I already wrote the obituary. You probably did, too.

Several weeks ago, Oregon dropped its third game of the season. That, historically, has been a cutoff to make the College Football Playoff—and the Ducks already were without quarterback Dante Moore due to a concussion.

Additionally, they still had Ohio State left on the schedule. Surely the Buckeyes wouldn't fall to a Moore-less Ducks team? Well, fast-forward a bit, and OSU lost its own quarterback to injury. Oregon ended up recording Top 25 wins against Northwestern and Ohio State in consecutive weeks, and Friday's rout of Michigan State pushed the Ducks to four victories in a row.

Crack open the coffin, my friends, because Oregon has arisen.

Yes, the Ducks absolutely must defeat Washington next weekend. There's only one unlikely path to the Big Ten Championship Game if UO loses.

As long as Oregon wins, though—and either UCLA or Indiana wins—it'll secure an improbable trip to Indianapolis with an automatic CFP berth at stake.

On Thanksgiving and Black Friday, the Lone Star State will host a critical showdown each day. Texas Tech needs a win to clinch a berth in the Big 12 Championship Game, while Texas needs a win and help from other results and tiebreakers to reach the SEC Championship Game.

The short version: UCLA can clinch a berth in the Big Ten Championship Game by beating rival USC. The remaining berth would come down to tiebreakers, depending on which of Iowa, Indiana and Oregon—all with two conference losses—win in Week 13. A UCLA loss would open up a much wider range of scenarios.

The Iron Bowl rounds out the weekend, with Alabama looking to remove any doubt about its playoff prospects. The Crimson Tide could still make the CFP with a loss, but a win would spare them some selection-day suspense and keep them in contention for an SEC Championship Game berth.

articles.title: Paul Merson believes Liverpool knew Xabi Alonso wasn't good enough - and we're seeing it play out as Chelsea manager
articles.summary: Chelsea have suffered back-to-back defeats in the Premier League and are slipping towards the middle of the table; the Blues have won just once in five games in all competitions; watch Nottingham Forest vs Chelsea live on Sky Sports this Friday, kick-off 8pm
articles.body:
The Blues were beaten 4-1 by arch-rivals Leeds at Stamford Bridge on Saturday, with the Blues now on a run of just one win in their last five matches in all competitions.

Chelsea have now slipped down to eighth place - and sit five points behind the top four. They do sit two points behind fifth, but Brentford could go ahead of the Blues if they win on Monday Night Football against Everton.

Merson believes Liverpool may have snubbed Alonso for the head coach role - eventually taken by Andoni Iraola - due to concerns about his pedigree.

There was no vacancy at Liverpool by the time Alonso took the Chelsea role on May 17, with Liverpool not sacking Arne Slot until June 1.

Read below for the Magic Man's thoughts...

'Did Liverpool see something that we're seeing now?'

My biggest worry is that Liverpool could have had Xabi Alonso and they chose not to. Obviously, Liverpool didn't think he was good enough.

Alonso took the Chelsea job and Liverpool sacked Arne Slot two weeks later. You can't tell me that Liverpool couldn't have spoken to Alonso and say: 'Don't take the Chelsea job, we're going to take you'.

He was out of a job as well, Liverpool could have had him and he'd have gone there all day long. So why didn't they take him? Did they know something that we're seeing now?

It just always sits in my mind. That was my worry - and now it's playing out.

If this was Liam Rosenior in charge at Chelsea and getting these results, he'd be in major trouble. One hundred percent, he'd be in trouble. And remember, Rosenior didn't have Morgan Rogers in his Chelsea team, bought for £116m.

But it's because of the unbelievable job he did at Bayer Leverkusen that everybody is thinking: it will be alright.

Tottenham and Leeds at home are Chelsea's two biggest games of the season for the fans - and they've lost them both. But while they're big for the fans, I'm not sure the players think that way. Not at all.

They probably think their biggest games are Arsenal, Manchester United and Manchester City.

The Leeds game changed when Moises Caicedo came off. For all the money they've spent… take Caicedo and Joao Pedro out of that team and Chelsea aren't good enough. They're the two players you cannot afford to miss.

They're not dominating football matches. The other major problem is defending. The goals they give away, the way it happens - it's mind-blowing. It's poor defending. Inexperienced defending.

The first goal against Leeds, Josh Acheampong gets stuck under the ball. I know he's a young kid but he still can't make that mistake. Then the ball gets to Noah Okafor, and Levi Colwill just jockeys to the side of him. He has to do something to stop that shot happening. He just dangles his leg out.

It's not be-all-and-end-all defending. You look at players like Dan Burn and Lewis Dunk for Newcastle and Brighton. They would dive in front of the ball and let the ball be smashed against them.

Sol Campbell, Tony Adams, Rio Ferdinand and Nemanja Vidic all had that mentality. Their job was to make sure you didn't score - and if you did, you'd have to produce something special to beat them. I just don't see that with Chelsea's defenders. It all seems far too easy.

We're talking about two Chelsea centre-halves, who are meant to be top drawer. One of them is an England international, and a future England captain not long ago in Levi Colwill. And then Wesley Fofana cost Chelsea £70m at a time when £70m was a lot of money.

Maxence Lacroix hasn't pulled up trees at Chelsea either. When he went off injured, it wasn't as if everyone had their head in their hands like if Caicedo or Pedro went off like that.

I expected Chelsea to get in the Champions League this season. Get in that competition and it's a great season. They're a million miles off winning the league.

The problem is there are a lot of teams above them. But now I don't see them beating Nottingham Forest on Friday, after what Forest did to Manchester City a few weeks ago.

That's a huge, huge, huge game at the City Ground. Every game you play for Chelsea is big, but if they win it - then I'd expect them to beat Crystal Palace after all and it's all looking rosy again.

They need Joao Pedro back. We go on about their front three. But if you had The Three Musketeers but took one of them out, you'd struggle to sell a film.

articles.title: Ashley Williams: Interim Swansea City coach leans on Wales boss Craig Bellamy
articles.summary: Ashley Williams says he has been in regular contact with Wales boss Craig Bellamy since taking temporary charge of Swansea City.
articles.body:
Ashley Williams says he has been in regular contact with Wales boss Craig Bellamy since taking temporary charge of Swansea City.

Bellamy was at the Swansea.com Stadium on Saturday to see the Swans draw 2-2 with West Bromwich Albion, in their first game since the shock departure of Vitor Matos.

Williams, who leads Swansea for a second time at Middlesbrough on Tuesday, says Bellamy is one of a number of managers he has consulted since taking the reins at his former club.

"I spoke to Craig [before returning to Swansea] and I've spoken to him most days as well which isn't unusual," Williams said.

"I've got a good relationship with Craig. Anything that I do, I would consult people that I look up to and he's definitely somebody that I look up to and lean on."

Williams in at the deep end as Swans look to steady ship

Williams to stay in charge of Swans for Boro trip

Williams became part of Bellamy's Wales staff in September, joining as an assistant coach alongside former Swansea head coach Alan Sheehan.

That was a first move into a senior coaching set-up for ex-Wales captain Williams, who has largely focused on punditry work since retiring as a player in 2021.

The 42-year-old says Bellamy is one of a number of managers influencing his approach to leading the Championship club.

"I've been fortunate to play under Roberto [Martinez], Ronald Koeman, Brendan [Rodgers], Chris Coleman, Michael Laudrup, so many really, really big names," Williams said.

"You take a little bit from all of them - you leave the bits that you don't like, and you take the bits that you do like."

Former Swansea and Everton defender Williams added: "I've been really impressed with Craig. We have long days on international [camp], he can be demanding but it's Craig and you'd expect nothing less.

"It doesn't become a chore because it's so fun and again just like now [at Swansea], I'm working with a friend - I consider Craig one of my really good friends.

"If anything, in terms of my first job to go in properly, the bar's been set so high now of how I see things working on a day-to-day basis, because I think he's one of the best."

'I've seen a definite improvement on TV'

Williams and Sheehan were brought in by Wales following the departures of James Rowberry and Piet Cremers.

The Football Association of Wales did not specify how long the duo would be involved, but Williams says he expects to be part of the national side's staff for next March's Nations League play-off against Slovenia.

Bellamy, meanwhile, says Williams has "so much to offer" as a coach – and believes he has improved since linking up with Wales.

"I've seen a definite improvement from him when he's on TV now," Bellamy joked.

"He's actually talking quite a lot of sense, whereas before, and he'll tell you, he's like, 'I knew nothing about football'.

"He got paid quite well and did quite a few gigs off [the back of punditry]. Now when he's talking you should listen to him because he's talking a lot more sense."

articles.title: Manchester United to appeal Leny Yoro's red card as ex-PL referee Dermot Gallagehr casts his verdict
articles.summary: Manchester United lost 4-0 to Liverpool in the Premier League on Sunday, with Leny Yoro sent off inside the first eight minutes for denying a clear goalscoring opportunity; the club have informed the FA of their plans to appeal decision; Dermot Gallagher agreed with the onfield decision
articles.body:
Mauricio Pochettino's side lost 4-0 at Anfield in the Argentine's first game in charge, and his plans went up in smoke as Yoro was dismissed inside the first eight minutes for bundling over Alexander Isak as the striker ran through on goal.

There was some debate as to whether the foul was a clear denial of the goalscoring opportunity, as it was unclear whether Isak was in control of the ball as he made his way towards the penalty area.

Under the laws of the game, one of the considerations regarding a red card for Denying of an Obvious Goalscoring Opportunity (DOGS), is the likelihood of the attacking player "keeping or gaining control of the ball".

United boss Pochettino felt that not only did Isak lose control of the ball with his touch, but also that United should have been given a penalty for Jeremy Jacquet's challenge on Bryan Mbeumo at the opposite end just moments before.

However, former Premier League referee Dermot Gallagher backed the onfield decision in both instances.

"If you look at it from the referee's angle, is it a foul? That's the first step. Yes. Is he in possession of the ball? From that angle, yes.

"I think most people would have expected a red card. It would have been a surprise during the game if a red card hadn't been given.

"I don't know if he would have got to the ball before Lammens. You watch it play out. Do you think it's a red card? Gary Neville's immediate reaction was red card."

On Mbeumo's penalty appeal: "When players are side by side, you can do that. They are side by side. Jacquet was even in front of him."

Pochettino: 'The ball was for the goalkeeper'

"The ball was for the goalkeeper. In that situation, if you review the VAR you can see for sure, [Yoro] never had the intention to connect with Isak.

"When the control was long with the striker, the ball was going to the goalkeeper, he runs and goes down. In Leny's case, it wasn't intentional.

"If you look before, on the sixth minute. Jacquet on Mbeumo. Similar? No. If you compare the actions, that was a penalty."

'No chance' - Mainoo fumes at penalty decision

Manchester United midfielder Kobbie Mainoo on the red card:

"The game's been taken out of our hands by a red card that I don't think can be a red card," he said.

"No chance. The ball's already with the goalkeeper. They're both running full speed. What can we do? It is what it is.

"It's 10 vs 11, you come to a place like Anfield, it's a tough game anyway. Then you lose a man, it makes it hard. I can't fault the boys for their fight in the game. We take the pain and move on.

"I wouldn't say it all goes out the window. You can still take the things you did in training into the game, but it makes it 10 times harder with one less man in a situation like that."

Sky Sports' Roy Keane speaking at half-time:

"Isak's not getting the ball. There's no way he's getting the ball.

"It's clumsy from United. Obviously it's one straight ball over the top. You shouldn't be in so much trouble.

"But there's no way he's getting that ball. Absolutely not. I know Isak is quick and he's sharp, but we've looked at it again.

"It's really poor defending. Players not smelling danger. But Isak is not getting that ball. Absolutely not."

articles.body: La segunda eliminatoria de la Copa del Rey ya conoce sus 28 enfrentamientos, que han sido agrupados en una división norte-sur. Las fechas de celebración de los partidos será el 1, 2 y 3 de diciembre y los emparejamientos son los siguientes: ZONA NORTE Sestao - Villarreal Portugalete - Deportivo Torrelavega - Alavés Numancia - Athletic Arosa - Celta Real Avila - Getafe Reus Reddis - Racing Amorebieta - Osasuna CE Europa - Rayo Vallecano Huesca - Girona Sant Andreu - Eibar Cultural - Castellón Ponferradina - Andorra Zamora - Valladolid Majadahonda - Mallorca Mirandés - Leganés Zaragoza - Burgos Sabadell - Sporting ZONA SUR Atlético Paso - Sevilla Cartagena - Elche Coria - Málaga Extremadura - Real Betis Antequera - Levante Real Jaén - Valencia Almería - Granada Albacete - Las Palmas Eldense - Tenerife Ceuta - Cádiz Los tres equipos más agraciados del sorteo han sido el Sestao, que recibirá en Las Llanas al Villarreal tras haber noqueado al Espanyol en primera ronda. Esta eliminatoria va a ser una fiesta". "Con esto se hace más feliz a la gente y son más próximos los partidos. La Copa es una competición muy bonita y un ejemplo es el Atlético Paso, en una isla que ha sufrido mucho (La Palma) y va a tener la oportunidad de disfrutar un partido histórico contra el Sevilla", concluye.

articles.title: Watford set to appoint former Romania coach Edward Iordanescu
articles.summary: Watford are set to appoint former Romania coach Edward Iordanescu as their new head coach, reports BBC Three Counties Radio.
articles.body:
Watford are set to appoint Edward Iordanescu as their new manager.

BBC Three Counties Radio report the Romanian is due to become the Hornets' sixth manager inside 18 months after they sacked head coach Alessio Dionisi following Saturday's 4-0 defeat at Sheffield United in his 18th game in charge.

The 48-year-old is understood to be arriving in the UK on Tuesday to sign his contract and plans to bring three members of staff with him and hopes to be in the dugout for Wednesday's Championship fixture at home to Blackburn Rovers (19:45 GMT).

Iordanescu guided Romania at Euro 2024 where they topped their group ahead of Belgium with all four sides ending level on four points from three games before a 3-0 defeat against the Netherlands in the Round of 16.

Iordanescu - whose father Anghel had three spells in charge of the Romanian national team, leading them in two World Cups and two European Championships - left his last role at Polish club Legia Warsaw in October 2025.

It was the 48-year-old's ninth club over a 15-year coaching career which has taken in Bulgarian club CSKA Sofia as well as Steaua Bucharest and Cluj among others in his homeland.

Dionisi, who departed with the Hornets in 21st, four points above the relegation zone, was only appointed in June after the departure of Ed Still, who himself lasted only three months at Vicarage Road.

Still, Javi Gracia and Paulo Pezzolano were all also given full-time contracts after Tom Cleverley left in May 2025.

The 46-year-old Italian was Watford's 12th head coach, not including interim bosses, since the end of the 2020-21 season, and leaves the Hornets searching for a 25th since the Pozzo family took over the club in 2012.

The club have had 57 permanent managers in their 145-year history.

articles.title: Arsenal's shocking WSL season analysed: No home win, a lack of goals and a disenfranchised fanbase
articles.summary: Digital journalist Laura Hunter returns for a second season with a WSL-dedicated column, analysing all the big talking points from across the weekend's action; this week's focus is on Arsenal's woeful form and why problems are likely to persist
articles.body:
Power struggles at the top present opportunity...

Before the weekend, there had never existed a time where Arsenal, Chelsea and Manchester City all failed to win on the same matchday. A turning point, perhaps? The rest of the division will be quick to smell the whiff of opportunity.

Because while Arsenal languish down in sixth and both Chelsea and Man City prove that others besides each other can rid them of points, the Women's Super League appears increasingly more open. This could be a race for the ages.

Of course ambitions come in all shapes and sizes. To measure against standards, there is nothing wrong with where the top two finds themselves, albeit patchy performance levels at the weekend led both managers to speak of better balance.

Andree Jeglertz went a step further. He described City's 3-1 defeat to Spurs as a "wake-up call", the first time his side have been beaten at home in the league under him. And their first taste of back-to-back defeats since January 2025.

But in an analysis led on the paucity of performance and standing, Arsenal must take the brunt. They have hit a new low this term and trouble is brewing. Is Renee Slegers' time up?

For a side that won the Champions League just 18 months ago, Arsenal bare no hallmarks of elite. They are grossly underachieving against the calibre of talent within the squad and Slegers' course of correction, so far, has proved futile.

The Gunners have tumbled down the league and are well out of the running for a European spot. But if just qualifying for the Champions League again is all Arsenal's season has been reduced to, one has got to question exactly how far they have fallen and who is responsible for such a rapid decline.

Arsenal no longer have the authority on which their reputation was built. Opposition teams are not afraid to impose themselves at the Emirates, rather, they are invited to. Arsenal rank 11th in the home form table having scored as many goals as they have conceded (4).

On Sunday, frustration peaked. Arsenal were booed off by sections of their own support after being held to a sixth successive home draw, this time to West Ham. Fans have had enough of the impasse. And while Slegers has identified the issue - "We don't inspire enough. We don't bring enough energy" - she is yet to propose a solution.

Territorially, Arsenal are sitting deeper, with less urgency to commit numbers in forward areas. Their central players are having far less influence in possession and therefore connecting the thirds with passes that cut opposition teams open is proving difficult. The injury to Mariona Caldentey is consequential in that sense.

Of course Arsenal still have creators. Their build-up phase remains tidy - but that's part of the problem. Where are the risk takers? Who is the player that sees the picture before opponents can react? Arsenal's patterns are slow and safe, rooted in keeping the ball, not risking it.

And yet, collectively, the Londoners have completed more final third passes than any other side and generated the second-most touches in the opposition box. Why, then, are they only just averaging a goal a game? That tally is fewer than newly-promoted Crystal Palace and Birmingham.

Another problem is that their only reliable source of goals is Alessia Russo. She is carrying an ailing attack that is systematically failing. At the weekend their conversion rate at the Emirates plummeted to just 2.8 per cent. Four goals scored from 141 shots taken is an alarmingly poor return and places Slegers in a difficult position.

It's clear her side are tactically stale but individuals are also failing to live up to the Arsenal name. That combination is hard to hide from. Goals have dried up. Wins are scarcer still. And Arsenal's once vibrant fanbase - the envy of the league - has turned sour.

Attendances have dropped off majorly as a result and will continue to dwindle until something happens to break this doom cycle. Slegers cannot afford for it to get much worse.

One might journey back to the summer for the root cause of Arsenal's rot. They were active in the transfer window, doing some solid business to bolster depth, but one opportunity in particular was causing a major stir. Did Arsenal give Alexia Putellas enough consideration?

Supposedly the club's hierarchy explored the option of pursuing a deal for Putellas over the summer but nothing got off the ground. Europe's marquee signing joined London City instead. You need only look at their elevated position to understand her impact.

The Spaniard has upgraded Eder Maestre's outfit beyond recognition. She offers a level of control and creativity in games Arsenal can only dream of. They have a higher competitive ceiling because of it. And more obviously they have newly acquired status and presence; Arsenal's replacement among the league's elite.

Perhaps signing Putellas was never realistic given Slegers already had Caldentey, and her squad is governed by a stricter wage structure than London City operate. There are no guarantees La Reina would be interested in such a move anyway. However, the fact remains Arsenal were not bold or brave enough in the summer.

That misstep has never been more apparent than now.

articles.title: David Raya injury: Arsenal goalkeeper avoids surgery and blow is not as bad as first feared, says Mikel Arteta
articles.summary: David Raya came off injured during Arsenal's Premier League draw with Newcastle; the Spaniard is the Gunners' undisputed No 1 goalkeeper with Kepa Arrizabalaga and Illan Meslier as back-up options; the 31-year-old got injured at a time where Arsenal have some big games coming up
articles.body:
Raya came off with a shoulder problem in Saturday's 2-2 draw against Newcastle and there were initial fears that the Spaniard could miss several months if he required surgery.

However, an MRI scan over the weekend has revealed that Raya does not require surgery and while he will miss Tuesday's match with Borussia Dortmund, more scans are needed on Tuesday to understand the full extent of the damage.

"He's not fit for [Dortmund] unfortunately, but it doesn't look too serious," said Arteta.

"We need some more tests tomorrow but it's quite encouraging with the pain he was showing. Immediately the action, we were quite worried but it's not as bad as we expected.

"We expected something much worse because he could almost not handle the amount of pain he had. The first tests we have done showed something much more encouraging. [On Tuesday] we need to ratify that to give you more specifics.

"There was no need for surgery. That was the main fear, because that would have ruled him out for months. Let's see."

Asked if he could return for Arsenal's big Premier League home game with Manchester City on Sunday, live on Sky Sports, Arteta replied: "Tomorrow we will have more tests. Then you will know."

Merson on Raya: Arsenal's next five or six games are crucial

"Raya's injury is a leveller for the other teams - not that much of a leveller because Arsenal still have some good players. When Chelsea miss a key player like that, that's it for them. But I don't think that's the case for Arsenal, they've got a very good squad.

"But that goalkeeper saves you points. That will be the problem for Arsenal.

"The next five or six games for Arsenal are decisive for them. If they come out of this run of games and they are five or six points clear of the pack, it's impossible for anybody to catch them. Every one of their next five or six games is a difficult football match.

"For me, Raya will be a miss. You'd be more comfortable going into those games with him in goal.

"He's the best goalkeeper in the world, by far, at making angles. He reads the game by always making the right angles.

"A lot of people don't see it. When the ball goes back to the goalkeeper, he'll always be on the right angle to get the ball - and then will always play it into the right player's foot.

"If Declan Rice comes short, he'll play it onto his right foot so the ball can go smoothly out to the right-back. All these little things help.

"And now it looks like Kepa is going to come in - and he's not played for a long time. And all these things have to work for him. That could be a worry for Arsenal."

articles.title: Man Utd to appeal Leny Yoro red card after Liverpool nightmare ruins Mauricio Pochettino debut
articles.summary: Manchester United have formally notified the Football Association of their intention to appeal Leny Yoro's early red card during Sunday's heavy 4-0 defeat at...
articles.body:
Manchester United have formally notified the Football Association of their intention to appeal Leny Yoro's early red card during Sunday's heavy 4-0 defeat at Liverpool. The controversial eighth-minute dismissal ruined head coach Mauricio Pochettino's debut, with club bosses adamant that referee Michael Oliver and VAR made a costly error.

United have officially notified The FA of their intention to appeal Yoro's red card against Liverpool , as per ESPN . The French defender was dismissed just eight minutes into Sunday's Premier League clash at Anfield. Referee Oliver adjudged Yoro to have denied Alexander Isak a clear goalscoring opportunity. The on-field decision was subsequently backed up by VAR, forcing the visitors to play almost the entire match with ten men.

The early dismissal proved catastrophic for United, who went on to suffer a humiliating 4-0 defeat . Club bosses have now decided to formally challenge the ruling in a bid to overturn the suspension.

Club bosses dispute clear goalscoring opportunity

The Red Devils' hierarchy strongly believe that the match officials misread the key eighth-minute incident. The report indicate their primary argument centres on Isak's control of the ball immediately prior to the challenge.

United maintain that the striker's heavy touch meant goalkeeper Senne Lammens would have comfortably gathered the ball before any shot could be taken. Because Lammens was positioned to intervene, the club argue that no clear goalscoring opportunity ever existed.

Head coach Mauricio Pochettino publicly questioned the call during his post-match press conference. He also pointed out perceived inconsistencies by comparing the tackle to a similar incident involving Bryan Mbeumo in the Liverpool penalty area, which was not given as a foul.

Dismissal sparks collapse on Pochettino debut

Yoro's departure triggered an immediate collapse on the pitch at Anfield. Liverpool capitalised instantly from the resulting free-kick, with Dominik Szoboszlai finding the net to open the scoring. With a numerical advantage for over 80 minutes, Liverpool comfortably dismantled their rivals to secure an emphatic 4-0 victory.

The result handed Pochettino a nightmare start in his very first match since taking over from Michael Carrick . The defeat compounds a miserable start to the campaign for United. Having played 11 league matches, the club now sit 19th in the table and find themselves mired in early relegation trouble.

The FA will now review United's formal submission regarding Yoro's dismissal. An independent regulatory commission will determine whether Oliver and VAR committed a clear and obvious error on Sunday afternoon.

If the appeal succeeds, Yoro will avoid a suspension and remain immediately available for selection as Pochettino attempts to turn the club's fortunes around. Should the panel reject the claim, the defender will be forced to serve a domestic ban.

articles.title: RedLac's rise: How gamer became an EA FC champion
articles.summary: Alfie 'RedLac' Calder's desire not lose to friends at video games led him to become an esports professional and saw him crowned eMLS Cup champion.
articles.body:
Millions of people have spent countless hours playing the FIFA video game, now known as EA Sports FC, dreaming that one day they might be in the game themselves.

For Alfie Calder, his dream took a different direction.

Rather than wanting to become a footballer, the 23-year-old has built a career playing the game itself.

Known as 'RedLac' in the esports world, Calder has gone from competing in his bedroom to representing Wales, winning the eMLS Cup and playing professionally for RBLZ Gaming, the esports division of German Bundesliga club RB Leipzig.

The title of the game may have changed, but the appeal remained the same. And Calder is proof that making a living from the beautiful (e)game is no longer a fantasy.

When he first told his family about his ambitions, not everyone was convinced.

"Trying to tell your parents you want to just play FIFA, they're thinking: 'What is he on about? That's not possible'," Calder told BBC Sport Wales.

"I remember my Welsh nan asking me what I was going to do for work.

"I said: 'I want to be a FIFA player, Nan'.

"She got upset and said: 'I just want you to be happy'. I think that was more of a sign [from her] that that's not really a thing, but all the best."

At the time, esports lacked much of the visibility and credibility it enjoys today. A career built around playing football video games sounded unrealistic, even to those closest to him.

Now, aged 23, Calder is helping prove otherwise.

"I'm representing Wales on the biggest national stage, making videos and getting millions of views," he says.

"I'm very grateful that's what I do and that's what my income is."

Calder's route into esports was not inspired by prize money or fame, instead it started with a simple obsession - winning.

"I started playing games online and I was losing to my friends all the time," he recalls.

"I don't like losing. I wanted to start winning more games and that's where my journey started."

That competitive streak intensified as he grew older. By 16, he was beating professional players and began wondering whether he could compete with the very best.

"I started thinking hang on, can I go and beat all the pro players and be as good as them?" he said.

"I never thought I'd get as far as I did though."

The importance of grassroots competitions

Calder's breakthrough came in 2022 when he won the EE Connected Club Cup at Wembley Stadium, a grassroots FIFA tournament that would prove far more significant than he realised at the time.

Trailing 2-0 in his first ever final, he fought back to lift the trophy and gain a confidence boost that would help propel him to the biggest title of his career so far.

Calder arrived at the eMLS finals in Columbus seeded sixth of the eight remaining players.

He went on to win every match on finals day to become champion and secure a place at the EA FC World Championship.

"When I played the eMLS Cup final, I did think back to Wembley," he says.

"It sounds silly because the context is so different, but winning that first final made me believe I was going to win this final too. I'd been here before and I'd won."

"The feeling was amazing, but in a way it was underwhelming," he said.

"After a few days I was already thinking I want more. Hopefully I can go and win something else."

Calder believes grassroots competitions remain vital to discovering the next generation of talent.

Events such as the Red Bull Wings Cup offer aspiring players the same opportunity he once had at Wembley, providing a pathway to the international stage.

"You don't have to be a pro player," Calder says.

"You can just turn up, have a bit of fun, try and qualify. Next minute you might be in Miami, playing FC27."

To many outsiders, professional gaming still sounds simple: turn up, play video games and get paid.

Calder says the reality bears little resemblance to that perception.

"It's only an esports tournament, people might say, but there's so much that goes into it," he explains.

And for Calder that sometimes is not as enjoyable as it seems.

"Naturally, [I play] 10 hours a day in the week leading up to a tournament," Calder said.

"That might sound fun but it's not really. It becomes like a chore because you're trying to improve constantly and if you lose a game, your head's gone."

Just like any other sport, preparation for a competition involves constant practice, analysis and exercises to improve reactions and concentration.

"You'll get a tennis ball and throw it to each other. It gets your brain wired and ready to go," he says.

"Half of the battle is mental. Your discipline, your mindset, your nutrition. There are so many things people wouldn't expect.

"I could eat whatever I want and turn up to a tournament, but I might feel heavy, play slower and my reactions might be off."

Perhaps the most surprising aspect is the role of a coach. Much like a manager on the sidelines, Calder's coach helps him identify issues he may miss in the heat of competition.

"When I'm playing, I get so locked in that I don't even know what's going on," said Calder.

He remembers trailing 3-0 in the opening stages of the eMLS Cup semi-final before turning to his coach for advice.

"He told me two things and all of a sudden I'm 7-3 up," he says.

Despite his success on the professional circuit, representing Wales remains one of Calder's proudest achievements.

His Welsh heritage comes through the same grandmother who once questioned whether becoming a professional gamer was possible.

With just the one tournament a year, Calder hopes Wales can build on their consecutive top-16 finishes in the next World Championships.

Most of all, however, Calder hopes his own journey shows young gamers what is now possible.

"The position I'm in doesn't even feel real," he says. "If I go out and someone comes up to me and asks for a picture, that's amazing.

"It just makes me happy because it reminds me that what I'm doing matters.

"Anyone younger who wants to get involved in esports should give themselves a chance.

"It's more than a hobby now. It's a career."
